synopsis: The 2017 EULAR/ACR criteria were built because idiopathic inflammatory myopathies are heterogeneous. In adults the most common subgroups named are dermatomyositis, polymyositis, and inclusion-body myositis; in children, juvenile dermatomyositis. Candidate structures included a count of items, a probability score, and a classification tree. The probability-score model discriminated best and was retained: points for the features present are summed, and the probability of idiopathic inflammatory myopathy is calculated with a formula that differs if a muscle-biopsy score is included. The probability with biopsy is 1 / [1 + exponential(5.33 − score)], and without biopsy 1 / [1 + exponential(6.49 − score)], or an online calculator can be used. The best balance of sensitivity and specificity was at a probability of 55–60% when biopsy was not included.
